title: Finland is about ten years behind Sweden and Norway in lung cancer survival, and the gap is growing
finding_en: Men diagnosed with lung cancer in Finland in 2020–2024 have a 5-year relative survival of 17.9%. The Sweden/Norway average passed that level about 10 years ago and is now 31.1%. The gap was close to zero in the 1990s and has widened by about 4 percentage points per decade (95% interval 2.2 to 5.7). For women the gap is 7.9 points, about 6 years. Pancreas and liver show the same pattern. Source: NORDCAN, fetched live by the analysis.
figure_alt: Line charts of 5-year relative survival for lung cancer in Finland, Sweden, Norway and Denmark from 1990 to 2024, for men and women, and Finland's gap to the Sweden/Norway average, which falls from about zero to minus 13 points for men.
